outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent includes a URL even though not explicitly required—harmless. (2) Minor wording like “destination: lunar flyby around the Moon” vs NASA’s “Crewed Lunar Flyby” is an equivalent paraphrase.

Critical issues: The only potentially critical risk is whether Artemis II truly qualifies as the “next planned” mission, because the Artemis II page DOM shows conflicting status-like cues (“LaunchED April 1, 2026” and “Occurred 5 months ago”), which makes the page read as if the mission already happened rather than being upcoming. However, this ambiguity appears to be an inconsistency in the page presentation rather than the agent inventing details, and the agent’s extracted fields (name Artemis II, year 2026, mission type/destination as crewed lunar flyby, and objective as first crewed Artemis flight/step toward Moon/Mars) are directly supported by the latest DOM state (state 5) on NASA.gov.

On balance, from an average user perspective, the agent did what was asked: it used NASA’s site, navigated to an Artemis mission page, selected the next mission in the Artemis sequence (Artemis II following Artemis I), and reported all required fields with NASA-backed evidence. The “next planned” wording is the only weak point due to the page’s odd past-tense labels, but there is no better alternative evidenced in the browsing session, and the mission details themselves are correctly captured from NASA.gov.
outcome.primary_intent: Identify, using NASA.gov as the authoritative source, the next upcoming/planned Artemis mission and report four facts about it: mission name, planned launch year, destination, and primary objective. A reasonable user would be flexible about exact phrasing/paraphrasing, but not flexible about picking a mission that is not actually the “next planned” one or reporting incorrect mission facts.
